gotchas.text: EAGLE speculative decoding is enabled (3 steps, eagle-topk 1, 4 draft tokens). Decode numbers in this cell include the speculative speedup; compare only against another cell with the same speculative settings.

The image lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38-27b is a purpose-built branch reporting sglang 0.0.0.dev0+qwen38.27b.g561c8f3, not a release. Its 476 parameters were introspected out of the container rather than typed, because the recipe uses mamba cache flags that no released SGLang version file carries.

QUANT=nvfp4 in this recipe means RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-BF16-LMHead. RadixArk also publishes an FP4-lm_head variant under a similar name and the two are different quantizations; check which one a comparison is against.

provenance.notes: NVIDIA DGX Spark (ASUS Ascent GX10, GB10) on Ubuntu 24.04 / DGX OS, driver 580.173.02, CUDA 13.0. Served with the MiaAI-Lab SGLang recipe (https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/Qwen3.8-27B-SGLang-DGX-Spark) at commit 751e29e, image lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38-27b (digest sha256:febfb971c7352570fc445c466ebd6ffc9d896024958e544a60f2137fd85856b1), which reports itself as sglang 0.0.0.dev0+qwen38.27b.g561c8f3. Recipe .env: QUANT=nvfp4, YARN=0, CONTEXT_LENGTH=262144, MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS=16. QUANT=nvfp4 selects RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-BF16-LMHead, the BF16-lm_head variant, not the FP4-head one. EAGLE speculative decoding is on with 3 steps, topk 1 and 4 draft tokens, so decode throughput here includes the speculative win and is not comparable to a non-speculative cell. KV cache is fp8_e4m3 and the mamba state is bfloat16. Thinking is ON: the chat template reports enable_thinking default_enabled=True, and SGLang parses it with reasoning-parser qwen3. The DeepSeek-V4-Flash service normally resident on this machine was stopped for the duration of the run. CPU pinning per the recipe (cpuset 5-9,15-19).
